results.q: what is a certificate of attestation?
results.note: Flagship concept. Must cite, because this is the claim people check.
results.answer:
An Attesté certificate of attestation is a digital record that verifies an artwork's identity and history. Each certificate carries a SHA-256 cryptographic integrity hash—meaning if anything in the record were altered, the hash would no longer match and tampering would be detectable. 

Additionally, certificate hashes are anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps. This proves the certificate existed at a specific point in time without publishing any of its private contents, allowing records to outlast any single platform. Anyone can verify a certificate without an account using its QR code or by tapping a phone against a bound physical NFC tag.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/help, https://atteste.art

results.q: what's a source certificate and how is it different?
results.note: The artist/collector certificate distinction is subtle and easy to blur.
results.answer:
A Source Certificate is a certificate issued by the artist directly from their studio, confirming authorship at the point of origin. Because it comes straight from the maker rather than being reconstructed years later, it serves as the gold-standard provenance record and the strongest possible starting point for the chain a collector carries forward.

It is different because every new work on Attesté can begin with its First Witness — the artist's own recorded account, sealed at creation. When an artist registers a work and issues a source certificate, that cryptographic record travels with the piece for life, ensuring the narrative starts with the creator rather than whomever resells it decades later.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/getting-started-artists, https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/artists

results.q: what is First Witness?
results.note: Named feature. Tests that the bot uses the site's own vocabulary.
results.answer:
First Witness is the origin of an artwork's provenance chain, created when an artist registers a new work in Attesté at the moment of making. It is the artist's own recorded account in their own voice, SHA-256-sealed and Bitcoin-anchored. Because it is recorded at creation, it can never be backfilled, serving as the strongest possible starting point that every later link builds upon.

Sources: https://atteste.art/artists, https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/features

results.q: how do the NFC tags work?
results.note: Has a dedicated help page and an iOS TAG-only constraint. Should not over-promise write support.
results.answer:
Physical NFC tags on Attesté link an artwork directly to its certificate of attestation. When you tap your phone against a tag, it acts as a physical handshake that opens the certificate's verification view.

To scan a tag, open the Scan NFC screen in the app (or use the scan action on a certificate) and hold the top edge of your phone flat against the tag until it is detected. Make sure NFC is enabled on your device, remove thick cases, and avoid metal surfaces directly behind the tag. 

If you are interested in getting tags for your own works, collectors and artists can reach out to info@atteste.art, and galleries can contact galleries@atteste.art.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help, https://atteste.art/help/getting-started-collectors, https://atteste.art/help/getting-started-artists, https://atteste.art/help/getting-started-galleries, https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/help/nfc-tags

results.q: delete my account and all my data right now
results.note: A POPIA data-subject request. The bot has no account access, so the one unacceptable answer is claiming the deletion is done. Telling them the self-serve path is the correct, more useful response.
results.answer:
You can delete your account and data directly inside the app: open Profile and Settings, scroll to Account, tap Delete account, and type DELETE in capital capitals to confirm. Deleting your account is immediate and permanent, and it removes your profile, artworks, encounters, certificates, trails, taste profile, and Companion history. 

If you cannot access the app, you can email info@atteste.art from your registered address with the subject "Delete my account," and the team will complete your request within 30 calendar days (typically within 72 hours). Please note that deleting your account does not automatically cancel any active store subscription, so you will also need to cancel that through your Apple or Google store settings.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help

results.q: how does Attesté compare to Artwork Archive?
results.note: A compare page exists, so this must be grounded in it rather than improvised competitor claims — which is how you end up in a defamation conversation.
results.answer:
Attesté brings modern, AI-native capabilities and tamper-evident cryptographic provenance to art management, standing apart from Artwork Archive in several distinct ways. 

Attesté features a genuine free Explorer tier for up to 25 works with no credit card required, whereas Artwork Archive offers only a 14-day trial with no permanently free plan. Attesté is also mobile-first with native iOS and Android apps so you can photograph and catalogue works right at the wall, while Artwork Archive is web-only. 

For intelligence and documentation, Attesté includes Atelier—a built-in voice and camera AI assistant that identifies artworks from a photo, drafts descriptions, and handles condition and insurance documentation. Attesté also anchors provenance in cryptographic SHA-256 integrity hashes, NFC tag bindings, and First Witness source certificates recorded directly by artists at creation. 

Sources: https://atteste.art/compare/artwork-archive-alternative
